description: Consistency cross-check across all six Sprint 3 Phase 6/7 artifacts (docs/phase-7-routing/sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json, sprint3_ar1_assignments.json, sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json, sprint3_implementation_execution_plan.json, sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md, sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md), mirroring docs/phase-8-alignment/sprint2_ir1_agent_flags.json's real structure and role exactly: story counts matched across files, no orphaned references, RS computation checked against Phase C's real findings, and every internal arithmetic claim (score means, story-point sums, source-citation counts) independently recomputed rather than accepted on the artifact's own say-so.
reviewer_note: Runtime persona for this pass was computed by the Phase 8 harness as consensus-agent (claude-global-library/agents/consensus-agent/agent.md, no version field in that file's frontmatter, read in full together with its 4 mandatory skills: ai-agents-core, agent-reliability-core, system-design, error-handling-patterns). That persona and skill set are built to peer-review architecture blueprints and multi-agent workflow plans against POMDP belief-state thresholds, token-budget math, interface-contract completeness, and failure-mode coverage before squad execution begins - it does not name Sprint-routing-artifact citation cross-checking, JSON arithmetic verification, or SRS/HLD/backlog consistency auditing anywhere in its own Role/Core Responsibilities/Skill Scope sections. This is the same class of routing/persona mismatch sprint2_ir1_agent_flags.json's own reviewer_note already disclosed for the Sprint 2 IR.1 pass (there, reliability-auditor was dispatched for the same kind of task); it recurs here for a different persona (consensus-agent) and is disclosed as a Phase 8 agent-selection-step observation, not silently worked around. The actual verification work below was performed to the letter of the task instructions, using error-handling-patterns' own retry/verification discipline and agent-reliability-core's DAG/cascading-failure cross-artifact-dependency framing as the closest applicable general method from the loaded skill set, since none of the four skills' domain-specific formulas (token-budget quadratic-growth math, POMDP belief update, Amdahl/Little's-Law system-design math, circuit-breaker state machine) apply directly to a documentation/JSON cross-check; every numeric claim below was independently recomputed with a script reading the real JSON, not estimated or taken on any artifact's own prose.
method: For each of the 6 Sprint 3 items (DASH-STORY-021, 022, 011, 023, 024, 025): (1) read sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json's 6 candidate_items entries and confirmed each maps 1:1 to an assignments[] entry in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json with no dropped or added item; (2) read sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's assignments[], p1_security_override, dependency_integrity_check, routing_gaps, and summary blocks in full; (3) read sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json's context_windows[] and summary blocks in full and cross-checked each story_id/assigned_agent pair against sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own assignment; (4) read sprint3_implementation_execution_plan.json's scope_note, execution_summary and determinism_guardrail sections and confirmed its 6-story/18-prompt (3 x 6) shape and its advisory_reviews_not_dispatched_here list matches sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own 4 open advisory-review decisions (SP3-DEC-101/102/104/105) with no story added or dropped; (5) read sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md and sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md in full and independently re-verified their own numeric claims against the real sprint3_ar1_assignments.json/sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json content using a script (not by re-reading prose), specifically: the summary.score_range {min, max, mean} recomputed from all 6 assignments[].score values; the per-agent story_points sums in summary.agent_load recomputed from all 6 assignments[].story_points values grouped by assigned_agent; the total_context_budget_tokens recomputed from all 6 context_windows[].context_budget_tokens values; and the count of context_windows[].sources[] array elements recomputed across all 6 stories and compared against sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md's and sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md's own stated '62 individual sources[] entries' figure; (6) grepped the real docs/phase-1.5-api/openapi.yaml for 'operationId:' to independently re-confirm the operationId count sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md claims to have fixed to 32 everywhere in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json/sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json.

per_item_cross_check.detail: sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json SPRINT3-CAND-001 -> sprint3_ar1_assignments.json DASH-STORY-021 -> sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json DASH-STORY-021 (assigned_agent python-backend-engineer consistent across both files) -> sprint3_implementation_execution_plan.json DASH-STORY-021 (implementing_agent python-backend-engineer, context_budget 4500 tokens matches ar3's own value). No orphaned reference; story_points=3 consistent everywhere it is cited.

sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json SPRINT3-CAND-002 -> DASH-STORY-022 consistent across ar1/ar3/execution-plan. dependency_integrity_check.sprint_3_edges correctly lists DASH-STORY-012 and DASH-STORY-017 (both real, already-landed Sprint 2 stories per sprint2_ar1_assignments.json) as this story's dependencies - independently re-confirmed these two IDs exist in Sprint 2's own assignments and are not invented. advisory_review (crypto-security-specialist, SP3-DEC-101) consistently OPEN across ar1's summary.open_user_decisions and the execution plan's advisory_reviews_not_dispatched_here list.

The one story whose acceptance_criteria field is a text description (spike_exit_criteria reference) rather than an ac_id-keyed array, consistently handled that way across ar1 (acceptance_criteria as prose) and ar3 (pii_exclusion_applied: false, the only story so flagged - correctly, since this is documentation-only research touching no zone). No orphaned reference to DASH-STORY-007/DASH-STORY-024 (both real, correctly cited cross-references).

per_item_cross_check.verdict: MATCH WITH ONE UNRESOLVED RESIDUAL DEFECT - see flags_raised IR1-S3-F1
per_item_cross_check.detail: Story/agent/context-budget (7000 tokens) consistent across ar1/ar3/execution-plan. AC-023-1/2/3 and must_not_deviate items present and internally consistent with DASH-STORY-025's own cross-reference about the eraseSubject endpoint not being presented as DPDP-complete. However, sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own invest.estimable field for this story still read '29 already-designed operations'/'(29 endpoints)' at the time this IR.1 pass began, directly contradicting sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md's explicit claim that 'all four "29 operationIds"/"29 wired endpoints" occurrences [were] corrected to "32"' and its overall 'PASS after resolution... 0 remaining contradictions' verdict. See IR1-S3-F1 below for the independently re-verified real count (32, confirmed by fresh grep of docs/phase-1.5-api/openapi.yaml) and the fix applied by this pass.

Story/agent/context-budget (7000 tokens) consistent across ar1/ar3/execution-plan. Role-name correction (dashanan_provenance_role/dashanan_episodic_role/dashanan_schema_owner replacing the stale backlog_draft.json 'dashanan_app_role' citation) independently re-checked: all 5 occurrences in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json and both occurrences in sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json use the corrected real role names - no residual 'dashanan_app_role' string found anywhere in either file by this pass's own grep. This role-name fix, unlike the operationId fix, was applied completely.

Story/agent/context-budget (6500 tokens) consistent across ar1/ar3/execution-plan. fr_minting_decision correctly traces back to sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json's own srs_fr016_minting_decision (no new FR-016) without re-deciding it independently - a genuine single source of truth, not a duplicated or drifted decision. zone_4_exclusion rationale (Procedure carries no subject-linkable field) is stated identically in ar1's must_not_deviate and is not contradicted anywhere else in the Sprint 3 artifact set.

dependency_and_reference_integrity_check.verdict: MATCH - no orphaned reference, no missing story, no cycle
dependency_and_reference_integrity_check.detail: All 6 Sprint 3 story IDs (021, 022, 011, 023, 024, 025) appear consistently across all 6 artifacts with matching assigned_agent and story_points in every place they are repeated (ar1's own per-story fields, ar3's context_windows[], the execution plan's per-story prompt blocks). dependency_integrity_check.sprint_3_edges was independently re-traversed: DASH-STORY-022 -> [DASH-STORY-012, DASH-STORY-017] and DASH-STORY-025 -> [DASH-STORY-020], both edges point to real, already-landed Sprint 2 stories (confirmed present in sprint2_ar1_assignments.json's own assignments), and no Sprint 3 story is referenced by any Sprint 1/2 story's own depends_on array - no cycle across the combined graph, consistent with the file's own cycle_detection: PASS claim. The srs_fr016_minting_decision is referenced consistently (not re-derived, not contradicted) by both sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json (source) and sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's DASH-STORY-025.fr_minting_decision (consumer).

rs_computation_cross_check.verdict: COMPUTATION ARITHMETIC CORRECT, BUT BUILT ON A CITATION-FAITHFULNESS INPUT (a=1.00) THAT WAS NOT ACTUALLY 1.00 AT COMPUTATION TIME - see IR1-S3-F1
rs_computation_cross_check.detail: sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md's own arithmetic, RS = sqrt(a x b) = sqrt(1.00 x 1.00) = 1.00, is correct arithmetic given its stated inputs, and 1.00 >= the stated 0.95 threshold does support a CONDITIONAL_PASS verdict on that basis. However, input 'a' (NLI source-level faithfulness, sourced from sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md's claim of '1.00 after fix... 0 remaining contradictions') is not actually accurate: this IR.1 pass found a real, unfixed contradiction (DASH-STORY-023's invest.estimable field, IR1-S3-F1) that existed in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json at the time the RS computation was performed and remains a genuine citation-faithfulness defect the Phase C gate's own 'all four... occurrences corrected' claim did not actually achieve. This does not change the RS document's own arithmetic (which is internally correct given its inputs) but means the underlying a=1.00 input was measured optimistically by one residual defect. Also independently re-verified: sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md's stated '16 acceptance-criteria entries' (used for its disclosed rule-of-three sensitivity-bound side-computation, not the reported RS itself) is correct - 5 stories' acceptance_criteria arrays sum to 15 entries (2+3+3+3+4) plus DASH-STORY-011's single prose acceptance_criteria field counted as 1 entry = 16, matching. Its stated '62 individual sources[] entries' figure (shared with sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md) does NOT match: this pass's own script-based recount of sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json's 6 context_windows[].sources[] arrays gives 11+11+7+15+13+14 = 71 entries, not 62 - see IR1-S3-F3.

flags_raised.detail: sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's DASH-STORY-023.invest.estimable field read '8 story points: a real FastAPI/gRPC host over 29 already-designed operations, wiring two already-built secure builders - large because of surface area (29 endpoints), not because of undesigned scope.' at the start of this IR.1 pass. This directly contradicts (a) the real docs/phase-1.5-api/openapi.yaml, independently re-confirmed by this pass via `grep -c "operationId:"` to contain exactly 32 operationIds, matching the already-corrected invest.independent/invest.testable/AC-023-1 fields in the same file; and (b) sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md's own explicit claim that 'all four "29 operationIds"/"29 wired endpoints" occurrences [were] corrected to "32"' and its overall verdict of 'PASS after resolution... 0 remaining contradictions' for C-1 (hallucination-detector) and 'RAGAS Faithfulness (citation-verbatim dimension) 1.00 after fix' for C-2 (context-faithfulness-engineer). The Phase C fix pass evidently corrected the three field-level occurrences it explicitly named (invest.independent, invest.testable, AC-023-1/AC-023-1.source) plus one occurrence in sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json's pii_note, but missed this fifth occurrence (itself containing two instances of the stale number: '29 already-designed operations' and '(29 endpoints)') in the same story's invest.estimable field - an incomplete fix silently reported as complete.
flags_raised.resolution: FIXED directly in docs/phase-7-routing/sprint3_ar1_assignments.json: DASH-STORY-023.invest.estimable's two '29' occurrences corrected to '32', with an inline note explaining the correction and citing this IR.1 pass's independent re-verification via grep.

flags_raised.detail: sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's summary.agent_load.python-backend-engineer.story_points was recorded as 24. Recomputing directly from this file's own per-story story_points fields for the 4 stories this agent is assigned (DASH-STORY-021: 3, DASH-STORY-022: 5, DASH-STORY-023: 8, DASH-STORY-025: 5) gives 3+5+8+5=21, not 24 - a discrepancy of 3 story points. The same error propagated into dependency_integrity_check.serialization_warning's prose, which stated 'python-backend-engineer holds 4 of 6 Sprint 3 stories (24 of 32 story points, 75%)'; the correct figure is 21 of 32 story points (65.6%), not 24 of 32 (75%) - the 75% figure happened to also match this file's own separate, correct story-COUNT concentration figure (4 of 6 stories = 66.7%, loosely rounded/conflated with the incorrect points-based 75% in the same sentence), which likely obscured the points-sum error from a casual read. devops-engineer's 8 and ai-engineer's 3 were independently re-verified correct (single-story assignments, no summation risk). The three agents' corrected story-point totals (21+8+3=32) still sum to the file's own correctly-stated 32-story-point total (dependency_integrity_check and the implementation-execution-plan's own story-points references), so this was an isolated per-agent attribution error, not a total-count error.
flags_raised.resolution: FIXED directly in docs/phase-7-routing/sprint3_ar1_assignments.json: summary.agent_load.python-backend-engineer.story_points changed from 24 to 21 (with an explanatory story_points_note field added), and dependency_integrity_check.serialization_warning's '24 of 32 story points, 75%' corrected to '21 of 32 story points, 65.6%', with the story-count-based 75% (4 of 6 stories) figure retained separately and explicitly labeled as a story-count metric distinct from the points-based one, to prevent the same conflation recurring.

flags_raised.story: N/A - artifact-level (sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md and sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md's shared '62 sources' figure)
flags_raised.detail: sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md states '6/6 stories, 62 individual `sources[]` entries' were checked and confirmed exact, and sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md repeats the same '62' figure as the finer-grained atomic unit for its disclosed (non-reported) sensitivity-bound side-computation. Independently recounting sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json's own context_windows[].sources[] arrays via script (not manual reading) gives 11 (DASH-STORY-021) + 11 (022) + 7 (011) + 15 (023) + 13 (024) + 14 (025) = 71 entries, not 62 - a discrepancy of 9. This miscount lives in the two Phase C/RS audit documents themselves, not in sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json (which makes no numeric total claim about its own sources[] arrays anywhere in its own text) or in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json. It does not change either document's substantive verdict (coverage was still full/non-sampled across all 6 stories regardless of whether the true count is 62 or 71), and the RS computation's reported value (1.00, from inputs a and b) does not depend on this figure - the 62-based rule-of-three sensitivity bound is explicitly disclosed in that document as a non-reported alternate reference point, not the reported RS.
flags_raised.resolution: NOT FIXED by this pass - sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md and sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md are dated historical audit records of a prior Phase 7 gate run, outside this IR.1 pass's edit authority (consistent with how the Phase C gate itself only had edit authority over sprint3_ar1_assignments.json/sprint3_ar3_context_windows.json, not backlog_draft.json's own stale citation). Disclosed here as a flag for whoever owns a future Phase 7 documentation-correction pass, rather than silently repeated or silently corrected without disclosure.

flags_list: Artifact-level (sprint3-phase-c-gate-results.md / sprint3-ar5-rs-computation.md '62 sources' figure), MISCOUNT_IN_AUDIT_DOCUMENT, LOW, NOT FIXED (outside this pass's edit authority, disclosed)
not_flagged_but_disclosed: Phase 8 harness dispatched this review under the consensus-agent persona/skill set, which is scoped to architecture-blueprint/multi-agent-workflow-plan peer review (POMDP belief-state thresholds, token-budget math, interface-contract completeness, failure-mode coverage) and has no stated coverage of Sprint-routing-artifact citation cross-checking or cross-file arithmetic verification; see reviewer_note above. This is the same class of process-fit observation sprint2_ir1_agent_flags.json's own reviewer_note already raised for a different persona (reliability-auditor) on the equivalent Sprint 2 pass - it is a Phase 8 agent-selection-step observation for whoever owns that routing rule, not a defect in the Sprint 3 artifacts under review.

sprint3_ar0_routing_index.json's own reduced 2-signal scoring model (domain_match/skill_coverage only, 0.70 threshold) versus sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's re-application of the fuller 0.75 assignment threshold to the same underlying scores is a disclosed, deliberate methodology difference documented in ar1's own methodology_reuse_note - not re-litigated here since ar1 itself already discloses and justifies it.

sprint3_implementation_execution_plan.json's word_count_band_note discloses that several Sprint 3 prompts (notably DASH-STORY-023/024/025's dev/qa/review prompts) exceed the reused 400-600-word band; this is explicitly disclosed as intentional (binding AC/must-not-deviate text is not compressed to fit a target band) in that file's own text and is not treated as a defect by this pass.
verdict: ALIGNED WITH ONE HIGH-SEVERITY DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED
verdict_scope: ALIGNED here means citation/reference/arithmetic-alignment across all 6 Sprint 3 Phase 7 artifacts: story counts match everywhere they are repeated, no story is orphaned or dropped between the routing index, assignments, context windows, and execution plan, every dependency edge points to a real already-landed story with no cycle, and the srs_fr016_minting_decision is a single consistently-referenced source of truth. This pass found and fixed one HIGH-severity residual defect (IR1-S3-F1: a stale '29 operationIds' citation the Phase C gate's own report incorrectly claimed was fully corrected) and one MEDIUM-severity arithmetic error (IR1-S3-F2: a per-agent story-points miscount), both now fixed directly in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json, plus one LOW-severity miscount disclosed but left unfixed because it lives in a historical audit document outside this pass's edit authority (IR1-S3-F3). This verdict does NOT itself certify Sprint 3 as execution-ready for Phase B dispatch - see execution_readiness below for that separate determination, which considers the 4 still-OPEN advisory-review decisions (SP3-DEC-101/102/104/105) and the 3 still-OPEN load-balancing/risk-acceptance decisions (SP3-DEC-103/106/107) that sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own summary.open_user_decisions already discloses and that this pass did not resolve (they are genuine user decisions, not alignment defects).
verdict_rationale: Every story ID, agent assignment, context-budget figure, dependency edge, and the fr016-minting decision cross-checked exactly across all 6 Sprint 3 artifacts with no orphaned reference and no cycle. Two real defects were found by independent recomputation rather than accepted on any artifact's own prose: a residual stale numeric citation that a prior Phase C fix pass incorrectly reported as fully resolved (IR1-S3-F1, HIGH, because it directly contradicts that pass's own 'PASS after resolution / 0 remaining contradictions' verdict and the RS=1.00 computation built on top of it), and a per-agent story-points arithmetic error that also propagated into a derived percentage claim (IR1-S3-F2, MEDIUM). Both are now fixed directly in sprint3_ar1_assignments.json. A third, lower-severity miscount was found in the Phase C/RS audit documents' own '62 sources' figure (actual: 71) but left unfixed as outside this pass's edit authority over historical records, and is disclosed rather than silently repeated.

execution_readiness.determination: NOT YET EXECUTION-READY - genuinely open user decisions remain, unrelated to this pass's alignment findings.
execution_readiness.reasoning: sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own summary.open_user_decisions lists 7 items (SP3-DEC-101 through SP3-DEC-107), all still status OPEN at the time of this IR.1 pass: four are non-blocking advisory-review authorizations (crypto-security-specialist for DASH-STORY-022 and DASH-STORY-025, api-security-auditor for DASH-STORY-023, cloud-security-architect for DASH-STORY-024) that sprint3_implementation_execution_plan.json's own advisory_reviews_not_dispatched_here list confirms were deliberately not dispatched pending that authorization; the other three are load-balancing/risk-acceptance/team-shape preference questions (SP3-DEC-103, SP3-DEC-106, SP3-DEC-107) that this file's own text states require the user's judgment, not a scoring model's. None of these 7 open items is an alignment or arithmetic defect this IR.1 pass could resolve on its own authority - they are genuine outstanding decisions for the user (Piyush Makhija), exactly as sprint3_ar1_assignments.json's own status/owner/due_date fields already state. The implementation_execution_plan.json's own status field independently confirms the same posture: 'PREPARED, NOT EXECUTED -- awaiting Phase 7 STOP 7 user review before any Phase B dispatch.'
blockers_for_phase_b_dispatch: SP3-DEC-101/102/104/105: 4 non-blocking advisory reviews recommended but not yet authorized by the user - each story's own must_not_deviate/advisory_review block states these reviews must actually run before the story is presented as fully closed/production-ready, not before dispatch starts, so they are non-blocking for DEV/QA dispatch itself but ARE blocking for closing the story

SP3-DEC-103: whether DASH-STORY-024 (FR-015) should be split across devops-engineer and database-engineer - a team-shape preference with no default that does not block dispatch either way, but should be decided before Phase B execution grouping begins per the file's own due_date

SP3-DEC-106/107: whether to continue deferring the python-backend-engineer concentration risk (65.6% of Sprint 3 story points, corrected from this pass's own IR1-S3-F2 fix) and the DASH-STORY-011 single-agent risk, both explicitly restated as still-unresolved across three consecutive routing passes per the file's own text
